subject: Subprocessor addition notice — Order Form clause sync
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudatlas.com, legal@cloudatlas.com
Date: 2027-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice of proposed subprocessor addition — CloudAtlas caching provider

Hi Avery,

Per Section 3.2 of our MSA (and the Order Form SOW), CloudAtlas is notifying Redwood of an upcoming change to our vendor stack: we plan to onboard NimbusCache, Inc. as a caching subprocessor for encrypted session caching. Nimbus will only handle transient cache keys and will not persist customer files.

Attached is the preliminary subprocessor registry (CloudAtlas_Subprocessor_List_v1.xlsx) and a short summary of the technical controls Nimbus provides. We expect to flip the integration on the week of 2027-09-13.

Can you confirm Redwood's flow-down requirements and whether you need an executed DPA addendum or an Order Form amendment to proceed? If you prefer, we can accept specific flow-down text you provide.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Best,
Elena Ramos
Senior Vendor Manager | CloudAtlas Systems
elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com
Attachments: CloudAtlas_Subprocessor_List_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 12 KB)
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Notice of proposed subprocessor addition — CloudAtlas caching provider

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the registry.

Quick answers:
- We need a DPA addendum for any subprocessor that will process or transmit personal data (PII) on CloudAtlas's behalf. From your note it sounds like NimbusCache will handle session keys but not payloads; we still treat that as "processing" because it involves customer session identifiers.
- For Order Form impact: if Nimbus introduces a material change to data residency, retention, or access rights (e.g., cross-border replication, logging of customer identifiers), we require an Order Form amendment that references the subprocessor and the applicable security obligations.

Looping in Legal (Lauren) for redline preference — I attached our draft OrderForm_Amendment_DRAFT.docx with suggested insertion text for a subprocessor flow-down clause. Priyom — can you advise on procurement timelines and whether we should request SOC2 Type II evidence or an equivalent security questionnaire?

If CloudAtlas prefers to sign our DPA addendum, please send your redlines and evidence links; otherwise propose exact flow-down wording and we'll review.

Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com
Attachments: OrderForm_Amendment_DRAFT.docx (draft)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-31T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Notice of proposed subprocessor addition — legal redline guidance

Elena / Avery —

Thanks for the details. I reviewed the registry and Avery's draft amendment. High-level guidance below; please see attached DPA-Redline_LB-comments.pdf for line-specific redlines.

Summary (Redwood position):
- Mandatory flow-down: Redwood requires CloudAtlas to flow down the same data protection obligations (security, confidentiality, incident notification, audit rights) to Nimbus. We will accept a written flow-down from CloudAtlas that mirrors Section 7 of Redwood's DPA.
- Liability cap carve-out: Redwood's standard is that liability caps survive flow-downs for third-party processors. We will accept language preserving Redwood's right to make a direct claim against the subprocessor where CloudAtlas fails to secure required obligations.
- Subprocessor approval vs. notice: We require notice in routine cases and approval for any subprocessor that will host or persist customer data outside the EEA for EEA accounts. If Nimbus will replicate cache nodes to eu-west-1, we will treat that as cross-border processing requiring approval.
- Evidence: provide SOC2 Type II or equivalent security assessment for Nimbus before onboarding. If unavailable, execute a supplier security questionnaire and agree to remedial controls.

Requested edits to Order Form amendment (high level):
- Insert explicit reference: "CloudAtlas shall ensure all subprocessors performing processing activities on behalf of Redwood are bound by data protection obligations substantially similar to those in the DPA."
- Add: "Notwithstanding any limitation of liability, CloudAtlas shall remain liable for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors."
- Add timeline: "CloudAtlas shall not enable any subprocessor until Redwood receives evidence and a 10 business day review period has elapsed (or earlier written waiver)."

Please confirm whether CloudAtlas accepts these principles or whether you propose alternate wording; if alternative, provide a redline. We want to keep this moving—if CloudAtlas can provide SOC2 and a signed acknowledgement by 2027-09-10, procurement will fast-track the Order Form amendment.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Attachments: DPA-Redline_LB-comments.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudatlas.com
Date: 2027-09-02T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Notice of proposed subprocessor addition — CloudAtlas response and redline

On Thu, Aug 31, 2027 at 08:25 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> (redlined DPA attached)

Hi Lauren / Avery — thanks for the clear summary. CloudAtlas has reviewed and we attached our counter-redline (CloudAtlas_Redline_Response.docx). High-level responses:

- Flow-down: we accept the principle of binding contractual flow-downs. We propose substitute language that preserves CloudAtlas's principal-agent relationship to limit direct claims against Nimbus to cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Liability: CloudAtlas requests a carve-out to the direct-claim right so that CloudAtlas retains primary liability; we can accept Redwood pursuing recovery against Nimbus if CloudAtlas assigns the claim, but we prefer to remain the direct defendant in first instance.
- Approval timeline: we can commit to providing SOC2 Type II for Nimbus by 2027-09-12; if SOC2 is delayed, we propose a remediation plan and interim mitigations (no cross-border replication, restricted key access).

We are happy to sign Redwood's DPA addendum if you can accept the liability carve language in our redline. If not, we propose a short call to resolve the carve-out and confirm the onboarding date.

Regards,
Elena Ramos
Senior Vendor Manager | CloudAtlas Systems
Attachments: CloudAtlas_Redline_Response.docx (docx, 22 KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@cloudatlas.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Notice of proposed subprocessor addition — acceptance path and MA plan

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the SOC commitment. Short procurement confirmation and next steps: 

1) Evidence: please upload Nimbus's SOC2 Type II report to the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CA-subproc-evidence-2027) by 2027-09-12. If it's not available, complete our supplier security questionnaire and provide a remediation plan.
2) Legal: Lauren, Redwood legal will decide on the liability carve-out by 2027-09-09; if unresolved we'll run a 30-minute escalation call 2027-09-10.
3) Execution mechanics: if we accept CloudAtlas's redline we will route an Order Form amendment via DocuSign. CloudAtlas to confirm preferred signee. DocuSign envelope will be: https://docusign.com/XYZ-CA-OrderForm-2027
4) Go-live: onboarding of Nimbus may proceed only after evidence is accepted and the 10-business-day review has passed (or waived). Target go-live window: week of 2027-09-20 pending sign-off.

Avery — please confirm commercial point: do we require an Order Form price change? If not, we will proceed with the amendment only for flow-down language.

Thanks all — letting legal and vendor coordinate next steps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
